arjun: heads up — eu-west2 dedicated pool started backfilling preemptible jobs around 02:10 UTC and we're seeing a persistent tail latency spike (~120ms -> ~420ms) on small genpar workloads :frowning_face:

marta: saw that too, noticed egress QPS went up at the same time. do we have a correlation id?

arjun: request ids in the trace look like `req-az-*-eu2`. quick grep from proxy logs:
```
[02:12:03] proxy: req=req-az-1eu2 latency=123ms egress_qps=600
[02:12:06] proxy: req=req-az-3eu2 latency=395ms egress_qps=1800
[02:12:11] proxy: req=req-az-1eu2 latency=410ms egress_qps=1700
```

jia: is this the dedicated slice that we recently allowed burst backfills for? might be saturating the rack egress link.

ben: yup it's the fractional dedicated slice config that has `burstable: true` for warmup batches. probably concurrent KV cache misses + tenant egress = bad combo.

arjun: can we temporarily turn off burst for that slice? `rbac` change is trivial but needs a deploy window.

marta: @ben can you toggle the slice flag to `burstable:false` for eu-west2-warmup? if not, we can block backfills at the allocator level.

ben: trying now — running:
`curl -XPOST https://allocator.internal/slices/eu-west2-warmup/toggle -d '{"burstable":false}'`

olivia: FYI this will reduce warmup throughput, might push preemptible queues to longer wait times. tradeoff: lower tail latency for prod. :thinking:

ben: done. allocator responded `200 OK`. watching metrics.

srebot: automated-alert: eu-west2 rack 7 egress utilization dropped from 94% -> 62% after slice toggle. tail latency on genpar decreased to ~150ms within 40s.

arjun: nice — looks like burst was the culprit. we should discuss a safer handshake for burst backfills: require egress headroom threshold before enabling.

jia: agree. propose: allocator checks 3s average rack egress < 70% and KV miss rate < 5% before allowing burst. otherwise mark slice as `backfill-paused` and queue for retry.

marta: also add a soft cap per-tenant egress credit while in warmup to avoid a single tenant saturating the rack. incrementally increase credits as KV warms.

olivia: can we implement that as a lightweight precondition in the allocator rather than full-on policy engine? low effort, high impact.

ben: I can prototype today. quick pseudo:
```
if rack.egress_util < 0.7 and rack.kv_miss_rate < 0.05:
  allow_burst()
else:
  set_slice_label(slice, "backfill-paused")
  schedule_retry(30s)
```

arjun: perfect. also add metrics/alerts for aborted backfills so prod owners can see when warmup is being rate-limited.

srebot: note: created incident ticket INF-2026-112 with initial notes.

marta: long term: consider moving warmup backfills to a different egress path (separate NAT) for large clusters. but that's infra-heavy. short term handshake + soft caps is our fastest win.

olivia: can we add a short runbook item? steps to toggle burst flag, who to ping if warmup backlog grows, and rollback path.

ben: drafting runbook now. will drop link here in 10m.

arjun: thanks — great fast mitigation. follow-up: propose RFC for allocator preconditions next week.

marta: adding to eng-infra agenda. :thumbsup:

ben: runbook: https://confluence.internal/infra/warmup-burst-handshake (draft)

arjun: closing loop — marking this thread resolved once RFC is scheduled.

jia: resolved for now, reopen if tail spikes reappear.
